targets.old_statement: A right turn on red is allowed from any street after a stop unless signed otherwise, while a left turn on red is allowed only from a one-way street onto a one-way street.
targets.statement: After coming to a stop at a red light, you may turn right unless a sign prohibits it, while you may turn left on red from a one-way street into a one-way street where traffic moves to the left unless a sign prohibits that turn.

correction.corrected_statement: After stopping and yielding to all pedestrians and all vehicles, you may turn right on red unless a sign prohibits it, and you may turn left on red only from a one way street into a one way street where traffic is moving to the left unless a sign prohibits it.
correction.note: Added stop and yield requirements and left turn traffic direction limit and removed any street.

targets.old_statement: A red X lane control signal means the lane belongs to opposing traffic, while a red arrow means stop for that lane just as a red light would.
targets.statement: A red X lane control signal means the lane belongs to opposing traffic, while a red arrow means stop for that lane just as a red light would.

correction.corrected_statement: A red X lane control signal means the lane belongs to opposing traffic, while a red arrow means stop for that lane just as a red light would.
correction.note: Red arrow rule is printed on page forty, not page forty-one.

targets.old_statement: A green light requires yielding to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection, while a right turn on red requires yielding to all pedestrians and all vehicles.
targets.statement: A green light requires yielding to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection, while a right turn on red requires yielding to all pedestrians and all vehicles.

correction.corrected_statement: A green light requires yielding to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection, while a right turn on red requires yielding to all pedestrians and all vehicles.
correction.note: Right on red yield rule is printed on page thirty-nine, not page forty.
